m5-t1.question: What is the correct first question in social platform selection?
options: Which platform has the most users?
Which platforms are trending this year?
Where do our customers already make decisions like this?
Which platform is cheapest to advertise on?
m5-t1.explanation: Platform choice = audience evidence + category fit + honest capacity; decision behaviour beats population size.

m5-t1.question: Why does the lesson say five half-alive accounts lose to one thriving one?
options: Platforms cross-post automatically anyway
Grammar differences, the recency penalty and effort arithmetic — five grammars at 25% effort each
Because platforms ban multi-accounting
Followers get confused between profiles
m5-t1.explanation: Each platform has its own grammar, platforms bury sporadic posters, and effort divides — one thriving account wins.

m5-t1.question: In the Kochi bakery's strategy one-liner, what makes it a strategy rather than a wish?
options: It mentions all five platforms
It includes the 'ignore everything else' clause — the decision about what NOT to do
It sets a follower target
It uses marketing jargon correctly
m5-t1.explanation: The strategy one-liner names audience, pillars, conversion path and KPIs — and closes the door on everything else until it works.

m5-t1.question: Which metric sits at the top of the value ladder (closest to business outcomes)?
options: Likes and follower count
Link clicks and profile visits
Qualified DMs, WhatsApp conversations, enquiries and orders
Story views
m5-t1.explanation: Vanity → engagement → traffic/action → business: conversations and orders are the tiers that pay rent.

m5-t1.question: For an Indian small business, which pairing reflects the lesson's platform-jobs map?
options: LinkedIn discovers; YouTube closes
Instagram shows; WhatsApp closes
Pinterest explains; Instagram does B2B
Facebook is only for teenagers
m5-t1.explanation: Instagram is the discovery engine for visual categories; WhatsApp Business is India's actual closing channel.

m5-t2.question: Which format is best suited to consideration-stage content that gets saved and shared?
options: Static announcement post
Carousel — hook slide, one point per slide, CTA slide
15-second trend remix
Live stream
m5-t2.explanation: Carousels teach, compare and prove; saves are their metric. Reels discover, stories build relationship, statics announce.

m5-t2.question: What does the monthly content-ops engine look like?
options: Decide and shoot daily, publish whenever ready
Batch-make monthly, adjust weekly, engage daily in a fixed 15–20 minute slot
Post everything on day one, then reply for a month
Outsource everything to an agency weekly
m5-t2.explanation: Make in batches, publish on schedule, engage in person — the system that survives exam weeks and bad days.

m5-t2.question: What does a one-page brand kit contain?
options: A full style guide with 40 pages of rules
Palette, fonts, a cover template, voice lines and photo rules — enough for instant recognisability
The pricing sheet and refund policy
A list of competitors' handles
m5-t2.explanation: Two colours + accent, two fonts, one cover layout, the voice sheet, simple photo rules: coherence at a glance.

m5-t2.question: Which part of social media must NEVER be automated?
options: Publishing at scheduled times
Cover creation in Canva
The human conversation — replying to comments and DMs
The content calendar
m5-t2.explanation: Scheduled posts plus abandoned comments equals a shop whose shutter never opens for conversation.

m5-t2.question: The café's account improved while doing LESS daily work. What explains it?
options: The algorithm rewards accounts that post less
Batching removed daily decisions, scheduling kept rhythm alive, and effort moved to engagement
Followers prefer irregular posting
The captions were shorter
m5-t2.explanation: Content ops is the machinery: one batch day, scheduled delivery, and 20 focused minutes of daily presence.

m5-t3.question: What does the lesson call the core arithmetic of public replies?
options: Every reply costs one engagement credit
You are never replying to one person — you are performing for the hundreds who will read it
Public replies reduce ad costs
Replies should always be templates for speed
m5-t3.explanation: Community management is customer service on a stage; the silent audience is the real recipient.

m5-t3.question: Put the four parts of a public complaint reply in order.
options: Excuse, denial, legal note, block
Name the person, own the standard, move to a private channel with a named actor, follow through
Apologise generally, offer a discount, delete the comment, move on
Escalate to the owner, wait, reply after a week, close the thread
m5-t3.explanation: So sorry, [name] — that is not our standard — WhatsApp the manager — then actually resolve it.

m5-t3.question: Why should genuine complaints never simply be deleted?
options: Deleting violates platform rules
Screenshots outlive deletions, and the deletion becomes the story — a graceful public reply is read by every future customer
It reduces the account's engagement rate
Deleted comments count as negative SEO
m5-t3.explanation: The audience watches how you handle the bad night; the reply is permanent marketing, the deletion is permanent suspicion.

m5-t3.question: What belongs on the escalation card?
options: The ad budget and the CTA
Who may reply, which topics go immediately to the owner/legal, the NEVER list, and the after-hours protocol
The follower count milestones
A list of blocked users
m5-t3.explanation: Deciding authority, triggers and never-lists in advance is the cheapest crisis insurance available.

m5-t3.question: Which of these is a community 'ritual' as the lesson defines it?
options: A one-time giveaway for followers
The Friday poll, the monthly customer spotlight, the festival UGC call — small, repeated, genuine
Replying to every comment within seconds
Buying followers on a monthly schedule
m5-t3.explanation: Rituals give people a reason to return and a shape to belong to — and generate the UGC and proof later modules feed on.

m5-t4.question: Why did five nano-creators outperform one 500k-follower influencer for the salon?
options: Nano creators charge less, so more posts ran
Influence is audience match × trust — the nano creators' audiences were dense in the salon's actual city and demographic
Big influencers cannot post about salons
The algorithm favours smaller accounts
m5-t4.explanation: The macro's audience was 70% outside Karnataka; five local, genuinely-engaged voices converted at a fraction of the cost.

m5-t4.question: How do you compute a creator's engagement rate?
options: Followers ÷ likes
(Likes + comments) ÷ followers on recent posts, plus reading the comments for substance
Views ÷ impressions
Follower growth per month
m5-t4.explanation: Engagement rate over recent posts, with comment quality checked — under ~1% on a mid-size account signals ghost followers.

m5-t4.question: What must a creator brief settle that beginners most often forget?
options: The creator's favourite colour
Usage rights — whether you can reuse the content in ads, on your page, and for how long
The weather on the shoot day
The creator's other clients
m5-t4.explanation: Paid ad usage usually costs extra — negotiate upfront, or discover you cannot boost the winning reel after it worked.

m5-t4.question: What do ASCI's influencer guidelines and platform branded-content tools require?
options: That creators only promote Indian brands
Clear labelling of paid partnerships — #ad or the platform's paid-partnership tag
That brands approve every comment
A minimum follower count for paid promotions
m5-t4.explanation: Undisclosed paid promotion is both regulatory risk and trust suicide; audiences forgive sponsorship and punish deception.

m5-t4.question: When is the right moment to ask for UGC?
options: Weeks after purchase, by email only
At the moment of delight — the delivery message, the table thank-you, the 'tag us' invitation
Only when running a paid campaign
Never; UGC must be spontaneous
m5-t4.explanation: The engine runs on timing plus incentive plus permission: ask at delight, reward with recognition, collect with a one-line usage permission.

questions.question: A bakery is on 4 platforms, all dormant, and asks where to advertise. What is the professionally correct first response?
options: Recommend a bigger ad budget across all four
Audit audience evidence first: which one or two platforms do their customers actually use to decide, then build presence there with a strategy one-liner and a stop-list
Start with whichever platform is cheapest
Post the same content on all four simultaneously
questions.explanation: Paid cannot fix dormancy, and five half-alive accounts lose to one thriving one — platform choice is an evidence decision.

questions.question: A campaign week has 4 reels, 1 carousel and no stories planned. Reels are hitting 2,000 views but saves and DMs are near zero. What does the format plan need?
options: More reels — the views prove it works
Consideration formats: carousels that teach and prove, plus daily stories with polls to convert views into conversations
Static announcement posts to break up the feed
A live stream every day
questions.explanation: Discovery without consideration formats leaks intent: reels discover, carousels convert attention into understanding, stories into dialogue.

questions.question: During the campaign, a customer posts publicly: 'Ordered 3 days ago, still not delivered, no reply to my DMs.' The page has posted twice since. What is the correct response pattern?
options: Delete the comment and DM an apology
Public four-part reply — name, owned standard, private channel with a named actor — then resolve and follow through; never leave it buried under new posts
Ignore it; replying draws more attention
Reply publicly that the courier is at fault
questions.explanation: Silence under active posting is the worst look possible; the reply is performed for the hundreds who will read it.

questions.question: ₹25,000 budget, local café, goal: footfall this month. Which creator structure fits the lesson's evidence?
options: One macro reel for maximum reach
Four to six nano/micro local creators at ₹3–5k each, plus boost behind the best performer — audience density and trust where it matters
A celebrity endorsement for prestige
No creators; spend it all on boosts
questions.explanation: Nano/micro creators dominate local campaigns on cost per result; their audiences are dense in exactly one place — the creator's city.

questions.question: A creator's 3,000-rupee reel performs brilliantly. You want to run it as a paid ad. What determines whether you can?
options: Nothing — commissioning the post transfers all rights
The usage rights clause in the brief — paid ad usage is a separate, upfront negotiation
Platform policy forbids boosting creator content
Only the creator's follower count
questions.explanation: Usage rights (organic repost vs paid usage, duration) are the most-forgotten brief clause — and Lesson 4.3's boost strategy depends on them.

questions.question: Which social measurement plan connects to business outcomes rather than applause?
options: Weekly report of follower growth and total likes
Saves/shares as engagement tier, link clicks and DM starts as action tier, plus 'How did you hear about us?' logged at every order
Counting story views only
Comparing follower counts with competitors
questions.explanation: The ladder: engagement explains, action indicates intent, and the attribution question ties conversations to orders.

questions.question: Your daily engagement slot is 30 minutes, and today there are 40 comments, 12 DMs and a complaint. Applying the reply matrix, what is the order?
options: Oldest first, alphabetically
Complaint first (1–2 hour standard), then DMs with purchase intent, then comments — spam swept and hidden
Comments first because they are public
DMs first because they are private
questions.explanation: Speed and severity are pre-decided by the matrix: complaints have the tightest clock and the largest silent audience.

questions.question: A brand's grid looks random and unprofessional despite daily posting. What is the fastest structural fix?
options: Post more often to fill the gaps
A brand kit: fixed palette, two fonts, a repeated cover template for reels and carousels — recognisability at a glance
Switch to a business account
Delete old posts
questions.explanation: Consistency compounds visually; a one-page kit cuts production time in half and makes the profile look curated.

questions.question: Which creator-evaluation signal suggests ghost followers?
options: A 7% engagement rate with substantive comments
A large following with under ~1% engagement and emoji-wall comments
Fast, professional replies during negotiation
Audience insights showing 80% local followers
questions.explanation: Engagement rate plus comment substance is the honest check — totals are rentable, conversations are not.

questions.question: A UGC engine is running but nothing is being collected. What is the most likely missing piece?
options: The incentive budget
The collection habit — a saved folder plus the one-line permission ask at the moment of delight
The hashtag
The camera quality
questions.explanation: The engine has four parts: ask at delight, reward with recognition, COLLECT with permission, deploy everywhere — collection is the habit that fails silently.
